title: Crypto Weekly: $40 billion error sees 620,000 bitcoins given away
summary: STORY: From a $40 billion error to disappointing revenue for Robinhood. This is Crypto Weekly.:: Crypto Weekly:: Bithumb's $40 billion errorSouth Korea's Bithumb said serious flaws left the crypto exchange's internal system vulnerable to possible sabotage.And that it failed to stop the mistaken transfer of more than $40 billion in assets last week.The virtual asset exchange said it accidentally gave away about 620,000 bitcoins to customers during a promotional event, instead of 620,000 won or $426.It triggered a 17% slump in bitcoin's price.Bithumb CEO Lee Jae-won said the giveaway amounted to 15 times the exchange's holding of 42,000 bitcoins. "First of all, we sincerely apologise to the people for the distress caused by the news of the erroneous transfer. We also extend our heartfelt apologies to our customers who have placed their trust in the Republic of Korea's digital asset market, to the lawmakers who work tirelessly for the sound development of the industry, and to the officials at the financial authorities, for the immeasurable concern we have caused."Most of the bitcoins have been retrieved by the exchange.But regulators say 1,786 had already been sold within minutes before the exchange froze the accounts of the customers that received them.:: Britain seeks to block HTXBritain's Financial Conduct Authority has asked social media companies and app stores to block access to crypto exchange HTX in the UK.The UK is stepping up efforts to prevent the group from promoting what it sees as "illegal" crypto asset services.The regulator said it also wanted Alphabet's Google and Apple to remove HTX products from UK app stores.HTX didn't respond to a request for comment.:: Robinhood's revenue disappointsRobinhood's fourth-quarter revenue missed Wall Street expectations this week.That's as a turbulent quarter for digital assets weighed on the company's crypto trading revenue.The news sent the retail brokerage's shares down.The California-based company reported record revenue of $1.28 billion during the three months ended December 31st.

title: Robinhood Offers to Bring Cash to Your Doorstep, for a Fee
summary: Robinhood Markets  is betting its Gen Z and millennial clientele are as eager to send out for delivery of a wad of cash as they are to order pizza or a pint of ice cream.  The brokerage is partnering with food-and-drink delivery app Gopuff to allow customers to withdraw cash from their Robinhood accounts and have it brought right to their door.  For a $6.99 delivery fee—or $2.99 if they have more than $100,000 in assets across their Robinhood accounts—users can skip the ATM and have money delivered in a sealed paper bag while they are at home.

title: Tech Weekly: Amazon's major outage, Apple's new record
summary: STORY: From a major outage for Amazon's cloud unit to Apple's new record. This is Tech Weekly.:: Tech WeeklyAmazon's cloud services unit AWS was hit by a major global outage.It knocked out thousands of websites, disrupting businesses and some of the world's most popular apps, including Snapchat and Reddit.The issue marked the largest internet disruption since last year's CrowdStrike malfunction.Roblox, Coinbase and Robinhood were among some of the other big names affected.Apple became just the third company ever to hit a $4 trillion valuation.Shares surged after data firm Counterpoint showed sales of the new iPhone 17 series performing strongly.Investors were pleased to hear the newer models were outselling the previous iPhone 16 series by 14% during their first 10 days of availability in the U.S. and China.European aerospace firms could be closing in on a major satellite deal to take on U.S. giants.Sources said Leonardo, Airbus and Thales have reached a framework agreement on a proposed merger of their satellite businesses.They have reportedly been in talks for more than a year to create a new manufacturing company - codenamed 'Project Bromo'.It would compete with rivals led by Elon Musk's SpaceX, which owns the successful Starlink.And Alphabet's robotaxi unit Waymo showcased its self-driving Jaguar taxi at an event in New York City.It was to highlight a partnership with the city's Bronx Community College to develop and enhance an autonomous vehicle training programme. Waymo and Jaguar Land Rover teamed up in 2018 to design and engineer the all-electric car.
